graph_algorithms.description: HyperQL graph algorithms are accessible via two distinct interfaces: Query-Level Canonical Form and Programmatic API.

query_level_canonical_form.description: Used within WITH and MATCH clauses. Results are typically returned as a node-keyed Map.
query_level_canonical_form.syntax: WITH AlgorithmName(NodeType, EdgeType [, option_key: value, ...]) AS alias
query_level_canonical_form.positional_rule: The first two arguments (NodeType, EdgeType) MUST be positional. All subsequent options MUST use keyword-argument form.

algorithms.name: PAGERANK
algorithms.signature: PAGERANK(Node, Edge [, damping: f64, max_iterations: u32, tolerance: f64])

algorithms.name: LOUVAIN
algorithms.signature: LOUVAIN(Node, Edge [, resolution: f64, seed: u64])

scalar_similarity_functions.description: Point-pair similarity functions used as scalar expressions in WHERE or RETURN.

programmatic_api.description: Direct method access on the database handle for use in host languages or UDFs.

pathfinding.name: shortestPath
pathfinding.signature: db.shortestPath(start: NodeId, end: NodeId, edge_type: EdgeHandle, weight_by?: FieldHandle, using?: WeightAlgo) -> Path?
pathfinding.description: Finds single shortest path. WeightAlgo: SUM (Dijkstra) | MAX | MIN | AVG. Default: SUM.

pathfinding.name: allShortestPaths
pathfinding.signature: db.allShortestPaths(start: NodeId, end: NodeId, edge_type: EdgeHandle, weight_by?: FieldHandle, using?: WeightAlgo) -> []Path
pathfinding.description: Finds all shortest paths with equal minimum cost.

pathfinding.name: kShortestPaths
pathfinding.signature: db.kShortestPaths(start: NodeId, end: NodeId, k: u32, edge_type: EdgeHandle, weight_by?: FieldHandle, using?: WeightAlgo) -> []Path
pathfinding.description: Finds K shortest paths (Yen's algorithm). Ordered by ascending cost.

connectivity.name: connectedComponents
connectivity.signature: db.connectedComponents(node_type?: NodeHandle, edge_type?: EdgeHandle, directed?: bool) -> Map<NodeId, u64>
connectivity.description: Labels each node with its component ID. Default directed: false.

connectivity.name: findCycles
connectivity.signature: db.findCycles(node_type?: NodeHandle, edge_type?: EdgeHandle, max_length?: u32) -> []Path
connectivity.description: Finds all cycles. Each Path is closed (start == end).

centrality.name: degreeCentrality
centrality.signature: db.degreeCentrality(node_type?: NodeHandle, edge_type?: EdgeHandle, direction?: Direction) -> Map<NodeId, u32>
centrality.description: Count of edges per node. Direction: IN | OUT | BOTH (default).

centrality.name: pageRank
centrality.signature: db.pageRank(node_type?: NodeHandle, edge_type?: EdgeHandle, damping?: f64, tolerance?: f64, max_iterations?: u32) -> Map<NodeId, f64>
centrality.description: Iterative PageRank calculation. Defaults: damping=0.85, tolerance=1e-6, max_iter=100.

centrality.name: betweennessCentrality
centrality.signature: db.betweennessCentrality(node_type?: NodeHandle, edge_type?: EdgeHandle, normalized?: bool) -> Map<NodeId, f64>
centrality.description: Betweenness centrality calculation. Default normalized: true.

community_detection.name: louvain
community_detection.signature: db.louvain(node_type?: NodeHandle, edge_type?: EdgeHandle, resolution?: f64, seed?: u64) -> Map<NodeId, u64>
community_detection.description: Louvain community detection ID per node.

pattern_matching.name: triangleCount
pattern_matching.signature: db.triangleCount(node_type?: NodeHandle, edge_type?: EdgeHandle) -> Map<NodeId, u32>
pattern_matching.description: Per-node count of triangles the node participates in.

similarity.name: jaccardSimilarity
similarity.signature: db.jaccardSimilarity(a: NodeId, b: NodeId, edge_type?: EdgeHandle) -> f64
similarity.description: Similarity in [0.0, 1.0] based on shared neighbors.

similarity.name: cosineSimilarity
similarity.signature: db.cosineSimilarity(a: NodeId, b: NodeId, field: FieldHandle) -> f64
similarity.description: Similarity in [-1.0, 1.0] based on a Vector field.

plugin_architecture.description: Third-party algorithms can be registered as UDFs.

performance_notes.description: Graph algorithms can be computationally expensive
optimizations: Use parallel execution where possible (PageRank, Connected Components)
Cache intermediate results for repeated calculations
Provide progress indicators for long-running algorithms
Allow query timeouts to prevent runaway computation
best_practices: Run expensive algorithms during off-peak hours
Consider pre-computing centrality metrics and storing as node properties
Use Node<T> for compositional containment; algorithms using (Node, Edge) signatures ignore Node<T> fields as they are not part of the edge-based graph topology.
Use LIMIT clauses when exploring algorithm results
Test algorithms on sample subgraphs before running on full dataset
